observations: Original SNL9 assigns three5/16×1⅛ steel countersunk rivets to each M359/M360 band; use twelve total for four forward ends.
The end fitting is visible at each removable free-end pin. A separately riveted fitting is a reconstruction interpretation; the catalogue does not separately number it.
HB154 connects long band to lever and short band to adjusting screw. It explicitly requires removing cotters and drifting free-end pins before removing bands.
Per long lining: eleven1-inch and one3/4-inch copper rivets. Per short: four1-inch and one1¼-inch copper rivets plus oneNo14(¼)-20×3/4 brass flathead screw.
The existing source registration is reused; the new fork/eye depth is not recoverable from that planar diagnostic.

Directly reviewed original SNL22 and restored orientation. The shaft-height section shows the high-speed drum beside its bearing; it does not establish the unseen rear bridge clearance profile or dimensions. The prior bearing review explicitly records that bridge as a coarse approximation.
decisions: Retain printed lining stock and existing clocking while fitting forward receivers; re-evaluate against the completed mechanism.
Represent each inferred end fitting as separate material with its three steel rivets. Use conditional25.4mm receiver width with0.25mm clearance per side.

Place longer lining rivets through receiving fittings. Extend the estimated M361 foot to261degrees to cover the first short-lining rivet and its bearing seat; retain the anchor eye and all rear coupling frames.
Fastener head forms and formed tails are engineering approximations; source stock-length datum remains uncertain.

Refine the estimated rear bridge with an R208 continuous brake-clearance recess over lining width plus 1mm per side, confined to local X[-225,-190], Z[-37,37]. This is an interface-driven approximation, not a recovered source dimension. Keep the source-sized rivets and lining stock. Verify remaining bridge stock and exact preservation outside the bounded recess, including bearing seats and fastener receivers.
